analysis:
Examined base lines 1014-1716 (makeEventStream, deadline-checked stream construction, native MiMo media preparation, tokenizer utilities) and head lines 1-525 (init paths, cacheScope/nativeLocalCacheScope selection at 442-443, prepareCompletion validation). The patch is visible only in part. Head 714-724 computes a reasoningPrefix for the vision media path from the rendered prompt tail via ReasoningPromptProbe.streamingPrefix, with contentSeed as a fallback. Head 747-749 passes stopStringScope from ReasoningStopScope to bridge.submitTokenized. Base 750-761 removes a block whose content is not visible; it likely moved prefix computation from after submit to before it. Base 1102 and head 975-976 and 1106-1108 are small changes in unseen regions.

Security-relevant parts unchanged in the visible text:
- cacheScope is still passed to submitTokenized, so T-041 salt scoping is unaffected.
- Release-on-every-exit and cancellation paths remain intact.
- The firstContentDeadline checks remain intact.

The reasoningPrefix only affects downstream parsing state. Per base 1287-1288 it yields .content(prefix) when native channels are not used. That prefix is prompt-derived template text from the provider's own render, not consumer-controlled raw bytes beyond the prompt tail. It could leak a think-tag seed into visible content, which is a correctness concern rather than a confidentiality one. It does not cross trust boundaries TB-002 or TB-007.

contentSeed applies only when seedsContentForUnknownPromptTail is set; that flag is true only on the local init (head 241).

For integration: verify that the head 714-761 region still invokes makeDeadlineCheckedEventStream or an equivalent cancel-on-throw path after submitTokenized, so the removed base 750-761 block did not drop a bridge.cancel or releaseBox.fire on an error path (availability / GPU pinning, T-010). Also verify the changes at head 975-976 and 1106-1108, which were not supplied.
